role: Benchmark suite for semantic graph query performance (indexed vs non-indexed).
detail: Establishes performance baselines for Neo4j semantic edge queries before and after index creation, with goals to detect regressions in Phase 3+ scale. Provides BenchmarkQueryResult and SemanticBenchmarkReport dataclasses to hold timing data. Core logic: _create_benchmark_dataset() builds synthetic taxonomy (WordSenseNode with IS_A/HAS_PROPERTY edges), _drop_semantic_indexes() removes indexes for baseline measurement, _time_query() executes queries with JVM warmup discard and returns median milliseconds, run_semantic_benchmark() orchestrates the full before/after cycle. Includes 5 canonical queries (scope_context_count filter, valid_to NULL filter, ancestor traversal depth 5, property_type filter, cycle check). Baseline performance table documents expected speedups: IS_A scope >= 3 shows 15x with index (0.8ms vs 12ms), valid_to NULL shows 14x (0.7ms vs 10ms), traversal shows 9x (2ms vs 18ms), property filter shows 16x (0.5ms vs 8ms). Safety gated: run_semantic_benchmark() requires use_dedicated_database=True to prevent accidental production use.
gotchas: Safety mechanism requires explicit opt-in (use_dedicated_database=True) to run; missing this throws RuntimeError. Benchmark dataset creation permanently modifies database (nodes prefixed bench: survive the run). Index drop/recreate destructive on any non-empty graph. Synthetic edges use scope_context_count=3 for high-confidence (i%5==0), otherwise 1; property nodes created every third concept (i%3==0). _time_query() discards first run for JVM warmup but includes in row_count (line 310-311 potential off-by-one if rows differ between runs). Cycle check query always targets fixed nodes (bench:thing, bench:concept_1_0), not parametric for all pairs.
